description:

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Recruiting Operations Specialist for Mercor NYC, you will own the operational core of how we hire - scheduling, Ashby, candidate experience, and on-sites - and you will be expected to automate the parts that shouldn’t require a person. Your remit is to define the core workflow, then build the systems that run it.

You’ll report to the Head of Talent and partner directly with hiring managers across engineering and operations. This is a New York role, in-office five days a week, in the Financial District. We’re a small team hiring fast, which means the scope is broad and your growth potential is what you make of it. The person who does this well will help define the function.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

INTERVIEW EXECUTION

- Run candidate interview experience end to end - screens, take-homes, virtual loops, and full-day onsites - across multiple teams

- Manage complex scheduling across candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers, and absorb reschedules and conflicts before they reach the candidate

- Treat interviewer capacity as a metric you own rather than a constraint you work around: track load, flag saturation before it slows a pipeline, and help scale the interviewer pool as volume grows

ASHBY AND PIPELINE INTEGRITY

- Own candidate data in Ashby - stages, tags, scorecards, written rationale - so the pipeline is trustworthy enough to make decisions from

- Build the checks rather than the cleanup: automated exception reports that surface missing feedback, stalled candidates, and inconsistent stage data before anyone notices manually

- Turn pipeline data into reporting hiring managers actually use - time-to-schedule, funnel conversion, interviewer load, offer outcomes

CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE

- Be the person candidates remember, at every stage - clear, fast, and human

- Automate the prep, not the warmth: interviewer packets, candidate prep, and follow-ups that fire on the right trigger without anyone remembering to send them

- Own post-offer coordination and the handoff into onboarding

ON-SITES AND EVENTS

- Run Superdays, candidate dinners, and networking events end to end - logistics, travel, comms, day-of execution

- We’ll partner to make the onsite a reason someone signs

BUILDING LEVERAGE

This is the part of the job we expect to grow. Over your first year, we want you to:

- Find the most repetitive work on the team and remove it - with automations, LLM workflows, Ashby’s API, or whatever gets there fastest

- Codify what our best recruiters do by hand into prompts, templates, and workflows the whole team can use

- Help us answer a question we can’t answer yet: which of our interview stages actually predict who succeeds here. We score every evaluative round 1-4 with written rationale, and nobody has tied those scores to on-the-job performance. That project is yours if you want it.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Salary : €5000 per month
Location : Poland (Fully Remote)
The role
You test the web application, frontend and backend, and the mobile applications on iOS and Android. That is the surface of the job.
Underneath it, the point of this role is to understand how the product actually works: the data flow, the API contracts, the places where two systems meet and produce behaviour nobody specified. That understanding is what lets you improve a specification before code is written, catch the gap nobody else noticed, and give Support, Sales, Product and Engineering an answer they can rely on.
We are looking for extreme ownership, the person who picks up the task nobody else wants because it needs doing and they can see why it matters.
What you will do
Test the product properly. Web end to end, frontend behaviour and backend responses, not just the UI layer. Mobile on iOS and Android against an agreed device and OS matrix, with a real understanding of platform conventions and where the two diverge.
Own our automated coverage on web. Extend and maintain the Playwright suite and write new tests for the features you take through. Investigate failures and fix flakiness rather than muting it, and be honest about what automation is and is not covering.
Verify at the API and data layer. Requests, responses, payloads, status codes, backward compatibility for older clients. Query the database directly to confirm what actually happened, rather than what the screen says happened.
Prevent bugs, not just report them. Pressure-test specifications with Product, Design and engineers before development starts: happy paths, edge cases, error states, empty states. Point out the platform that was forgotten, the API version that will break, the migration nobody planned. Asking the awkward question early is part of the job.
Debug to root cause. "It doesn't work" is not a bug report. Narrow down where it breaks and what the system is actually doing, and hand the developer something they can act on.
Support the wider business. Reproduce and triage customer issues that reach engineering, and keep test plans and known-issue lists current so release decisions rest on evidence.

• Mobile testing in practice. You can tell a platform convention apart from a defect, and reason about the device and OS coverage a given change actually needs.
